correctness.rationale: PASS for repairs/1/RESULT.md. The frozen Finding's unqualified sign-extremizer sentence overstates the result for L1. In C6, row j has entries ±1/4 at j−2,j+2 and zeros elsewhere; on a sign input each three-index parity class has at most two unequal pairs, so the normalized L1 output is at most 1/3, strictly below the L1 norm 1/2. Independent exact enumeration of the 64 six-cycle sign vectors also gave maximum 1/3. The corrected statement restricts the sign construction to L∞ and gives a point mass at a maximizing column for L1. For both norms the count follows from subtracting equal-sized supports of size d^2 with common support of size 2d−1+c4(e), and using skew-symmetry. If all rows vanish, each edge's two neighborhood sets form a saturated K_{d,d} component; the reverse follows from the same intersection count. Hall decomposition of a larger prime-plane incidence graph preserves four-cycle-freeness and attains the sharp bound for every degree. On the plane, normalized endpoint indicator bases have cross-Gram matrix A/(q+1), with AA^T=qI+J. Each nonconstant two-projection block gives s sqrt(1−s^2) at s=sqrt(q)/(q+1), yielding the stated exact Hilbert norm and separation. The supplied verifier was inspected, not run: direct composition is restricted to examples of at most 60 edges; exact row sums and the incidence Gram checks are finite evidence. The repaired proof independently covers the universal statements and the six-cycle counterexample.
